boundsProposal: Node.psql/psql_rc: the container command runs as `exec timeout --foreground -s KILL <t>`; PGOPTIONS sets statement_timeout=<t> and lock_timeout=30s; host timeout t+15; the default t is 300 s (profile psql_timeout_seconds). The previous default was unbounded.
cmd_backup pg_dump: `exec timeout --foreground -s KILL <t>` plus --lock-wait-timeout=30000; t = profile dump_timeout_seconds (default 1800); host timeout t+60, which dies with a clear message.
Exact per-run tag PGAPPNAME=replicactl-<RUN_ID>, printed to stderr at start and included in die(). Any manual cleanup uses only that exact tag. No pid kills and no inference by tool name.
Before anything stops (in guard, for the 4 mutating steps): a GNU coreutils timeout must exist in the container.
systemctl is-active/start/stop get host timeouts of 30, 120 and stop+60 s.
Whole seconds >= 1 (secs()): a 0 would disable both timeout(1) and statement_timeout.
